definition_en: in the most basic and important way
core_image: 剥掉层层外壳，露出最里面的核
scene: 这两种方案本质上是一样的，只是说法不同。The two plans are essentially the same, just described in different words.
sceneCN: 这里 essentially 是「本质上」（第 1 个义项：就最根本的性质而言）；句意：这两种方案本质上是一样的，只是说法不同。

senses.title: In basic nature
senses.definition: in the most basic and important way
senses.definitionCN: 就最根本、最重要的方面而言
senses.example: The two theories are essentially the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种理论本质上相同。
senses.why: The adverb strips away surface differences to show the inner nature.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词剥去表面差异，露出内在本质。

senses.title: In practice
senses.definition: used to say what something really amounts to
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某事物实际上等于什么
senses.example: The job is essentially about listening to people.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作实际上就是倾听人们说话。
senses.why: Saying what something really is brings the idea down to its effect.
senses.whyCN: 说明某事物究竟是什么，就是把概念落到实际效果上。

intro.en: Essentially is essential plus -ly, from Latin essentia, being.
intro.cn: essentially 由 essential 加 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 essentia（存在）。

items.en: Essentia means being or nature.
Essentialis means of the essence.
Essential enters English as an adjective.
items.cn: essential 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly forms essentially.
The adverb softens a claim to its core truth.
items.cn: 这个副词把断言收拢到核心真实。

note.en: Essentially is close to basically and fundamentally.
note.cn: essentially 与 basically、fundamentally 相近。

entries.definition: in the main or most basic way
in a basic and important way
in practice, almost the same as

normalIntro.en: Essentially points to the kernel under the shell of details.
normalIntro.cn: essentially 指向细节外壳下的那个核。

normal.en: Essentially the same means different in details only.
normal.cn: essentially the same 意为只是细节不同。

normal.en: Essentially unchanged means no real change happened.
normal.cn: essentially unchanged 意为没有真正改变。

normal.en: Essentially correct means right in the main points.
normal.cn: essentially correct 意为主要方面正确。

normal.en: The word often softens a strong claim.
normal.cn: 这个词常用来缓和强烈的断言。

normal.en: Compare basically: basically is looser, essentially points to essence.
normal.cn: 对比 basically：basically 更宽松，essentially 指向本质。

abstract.en: Picture peeling an onion down to its center.
abstract.cn: 想象把洋葱一层层剥到中心。

abstract.en: Imagine two roads that meet at the same point.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路最终汇到同一点。

abstract.en: Think of two cups of different shape holding the same tea.
abstract.cn: 想象两只形状不同的杯子装着同样的茶。

examples.en: The two designs are essentially the same.
examples.cn: 这两个设计本质上相同。

examples.en: Her answer was essentially correct.
examples.cn: 她的回答基本上是正确的。

examples.en: The problem is essentially one of trust.
examples.cn: 这个问题本质上是信任问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「essential（本质的）＋ ly」——从本质上来看，就是「基本上」；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 essentia（存在、本性）→ essential（本质的）＋ -ly → essentially，核心义「从最根本的性质看」。

sensesIntro.en: Essentially first points to basic nature, and then to what something really amounts to in practice.
sensesIntro.cn: essentially 先指向基本性质，再指向事物在实际中究竟等于什么。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the kernel left after every outer layer is removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：剥掉所有外层后剩下的核。

branches.en: The first sense looks at the inner nature.
branches.cn: 首要义项看的是内在性质。

branches.en: The second sense says what a thing really is.
branches.cn: 第二个义项说明事物实际上是什么。

branches.en: What something really is follows from its nature.
branches.cn: 事物实际上是什么，由其本性决定。

branches.en: The adverb often reduces surface differences.
branches.cn: 这个副词常用来消解表面差异。

branches.en: It also softens a claim to its main truth.
branches.cn: 它也把断言缓和到主要真实。

intro.en: Essentially is essential plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: essentially 是 essential 加副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Essentia, being, underlies essential and essentially.
latinIntro.cn: essentia（存在）是 essential 与 essentially 的根基。

items.example: Esse gives the idea of being.

definition_en: to start an organization or system, or to prove something is true
core_image: 打下第一根桩，让一座建筑稳稳立在地上
scene: 这所大学建立于一百多年前，最初只有两个系。The university was established over a hundred years ago with only two departments.
sceneCN: 这里 establish 是「建立」（第 1 个义项：创办机构或制度）；句意：这所大学建立于一百多年前，最初只有两个系。

senses.title: Set up an organization
senses.definition: to start a company, school or system that will continue
senses.definitionCN: 创办一个将持续运作的公司、学校或制度
senses.example: They established a school in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在村里创办了一所学校。
senses.why: The Latin source means to make stable, so establishing puts something on a firm base.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为使稳固，因此 establish 就是把事物放在坚实的基础上。

senses.title: Make accepted or secure
senses.definition: to make something accepted, respected or secure
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物被接受、受尊重或稳固下来
senses.example: The team established a strong lead.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍确立了明显的领先优势。
senses.why: What stands firm is secure, so establishing also means settling something firmly.
senses.whyCN: 站得稳就是稳固，因此 establish 也指把事物牢牢确定下来。

senses.title: Prove or find out
senses.definition: to discover or prove facts with evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用证据发现或证明事实
senses.example: Police are trying to establish the cause of the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正努力查明火灾原因。
senses.why: A fact placed on firm evidence is established beyond doubt.
senses.whyCN: 建立在坚实证据上的事实，就被毫无疑问地确立了。

intro.en: Establish comes from Old French establir, from Latin stabilire, to make stable.
intro.cn: establish 源自古法语 establir，源自拉丁语 stabilire（使稳固）。

items.en: Stare means to stand.
Stabilire means to make stable.
Establir means to set up firmly.
Establish covers founding and proving.
Established also describes long-accepted things.
items.cn: established 也描述长期被接受的事物。

note.en: Establish is close to found and set up, and shares a root with stable.
note.cn: establish 与创立、设立相近，并与 stable 同根。

entries.definition: to show that something is true

normalIntro.en: Establish is about a stable table: once its legs are firm, it stands.
normalIntro.cn: establish 就像一张稳固的桌子：腿站稳了，它就立住了。

normal.en: Establish a company means bring a new business into being.
normal.cn: establish a company 意为让新企业诞生。

normal.en: Establish contact means make a connection.
normal.cn: establish contact 意为建立联系。

normal.en: Establish the facts means find out what really happened.
normal.cn: establish the facts 意为查明真实情况。

normal.en: A well established habit is hard to break.
normal.cn: well established 的习惯很难改掉。

normal.en: Compare found: found starts an institution, establish also makes it secure.
normal.cn: 对比 found：found 侧重创办，establish 还强调使其稳固。

abstract.en: Picture a cornerstone laid before any wall rises.
abstract.cn: 想象墙还没砌起就先放好的基石。

abstract.en: Imagine roots spreading deep under a young tree.
abstract.cn: 想象树根在幼树下方深深蔓延。

abstract.en: Think of a flag planted firmly on a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象旗帜牢牢插在山顶。

examples.en: The charity was established in 1990.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构成立于一九九零年。

examples.en: She quickly established herself as a leader.
examples.cn: 她很快确立了自己作为领导者的地位。

examples.en: Experts have not yet established the cause.
examples.cn: 专家尚未查明原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ stable（稳固的）＋ ish」——让事物稳稳立出来，就是建立；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站）→ stabilire（使稳固）→ 古法语 establir → establish，核心义「让事物稳稳站住、扎下根」。

sensesIntro.en: Establish first means found an organization, then make something secure, and finally prove a fact.
sensesIntro.cn: establish 先指创办机构，再指使某事物稳固，最后指证实事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a first post driven deep so a building can stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一根桩深深打入，让建筑得以立起。

branches.en: Founding gives an organization its start.
branches.cn: 创办给机构一个开始。

branches.en: Making something secure gives it a firm place.
branches.cn: 使事物稳固，就是给它一个坚实的位置。

branches.en: Facts established by evidence stand firm.
branches.cn: 由证据确立的事实站得住脚。

branches.en: A new institution must become established to last.
branches.cn: 新机构必须站稳才能长久。

branches.en: A proven claim is an established claim.
branches.cn: 被证明的论断就是已确立的论断。

intro.en: Establish is built on Latin stabilis, steady, and the verb ending -ish.
intro.cn: establish 建立在拉丁语 stabilis（稳固的）与动词词尾 -ish 之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin stabilire means to make stable, from stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stabilire 意为使稳固，来自 stare（站立）。

items.example: Stare gives the idea of standing.
Stabilis means able to stand firm.
Old French establir carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 establir 传递了该词。

definition_zh: 建立；机构；企业；权势集团
definition_en: the act of starting something, or an organization that has been set up
core_image: 一座刚落成的楼房，门口挂上了正式的招牌
scene: 这家小餐馆从一家街边摊发展为当地有名的餐饮机构。The small restaurant grew from a street stall into a well known local establishment.
sceneCN: 这里 establishment 是「机构；企业」（第 2 个义项：已建立并运作的组织或场所）；句意：这家小餐馆从一家街边摊发展为当地有名的餐饮机构。

pos.zh: 建立；机构；企业；权势集团

senses.title: The act of founding
senses.definition: the act of starting an organization or system
senses.definitionCN: 创办组织或制度的行为
senses.example: The establishment of the park took ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园的建立花了十年。
senses.why: The noun names the action behind the verb establish.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词 establish 背后的行为。

senses.title: An organization or business
senses.definition: a company, school or other organized body
senses.definitionCN: 公司、学校或其他有组织的机构
senses.example: The hotel is a family-run establishment.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店是家族经营的机构。
senses.why: Something that has been set up and stands on its own is an establishment.
senses.whyCN: 被设立起来并独立运作的东西，就是一个机构。

senses.title: The ruling group
senses.definition: the powerful people who control a society or field
senses.definitionCN: 控制社会或某一领域的有权势者
senses.example: The young writer challenged the literary establishment.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻作家挑战了文学界的权势集团。
senses.why: The long-established powers are themselves called the establishment.
senses.whyCN: 长期稳固掌权的群体本身就被称为 establishment。

intro.en: Establishment is establish plus -ment, from Latin stabilire, to make stable.
intro.cn: establishment 是 establish 加 -ment，源自拉丁语 stabilire（使稳固）。

items.en: Stabilire means to make stable.
Establir means to set up.
Establishment names the act of founding.
It also names businesses and institutions.
The Establishment means the ruling elite.
items.cn: the Establishment 指掌权的精英集团。

note.en: Establishment is the noun of establish, close to institution and organization.
note.cn: establishment 是 establish 的名词，与机构、组织相近。

entries.definition: the building used by a business

normalIntro.en: Establishment is the building left standing after the founding work is done.
normalIntro.cn: establishment 就是创办完成后仍然矗立的那栋建筑。

normal.en: The establishment of a school is its founding.
normal.cn: 学校的 establishment 就是它的创立。

normal.en: A business establishment is a place that does business.
normal.cn: business establishment 是做生意的场所。

normal.en: An educational establishment is a school or college.
normal.cn: educational establishment 指学校或学院。

normal.en: The political establishment means those already in power.
normal.cn: political establishment 指已经掌权的人。

normal.en: Compare institution: an institution is bigger, an establishment can be a single shop.
normal.cn: 对比 institution：institution 更大，establishment 可以只是一家店。

abstract.en: Picture a new sign hanging above a freshly painted door.
abstract.cn: 想象新刷的门上挂起一块新招牌。

abstract.en: Imagine a table where the same powerful people always sit.
abstract.cn: 想象一张总是坐着同一批有权势者的桌子。

abstract.en: Think of roots that have held a tree for a century.
abstract.cn: 想象支撑一棵树百年的根。

examples.en: The establishment of the fund helped many families.
examples.cn: 该基金的建立帮助了许多家庭。

examples.en: This is one of the oldest establishments in town.
examples.cn: 这是城里最古老的机构之一。

examples.en: He became a critic of the cultural establishment.
examples.cn: 他成了文化权势集团的批评者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「establish（建立）＋ ment」——建立起来并一直运作的东西，就是机构；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stabilire（使稳固）→ establish（建立）＋ -ment → establishment，核心义「被稳固设立起来的事物」。

sensesIntro.en: Establishment first names the founding act, then the organization founded, and finally the long-ruling elite.
sensesIntro.cn: establishment 先指建立行为，再指所建立的机构，最后指长期掌权的精英。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finished building with its official sign in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：落成并挂上正式招牌的建筑。

branches.en: The act of founding is the first sense.
branches.cn: 创立的动作是首要义项。

branches.en: The thing founded becomes an organization.
branches.cn: 被创立的东西成为机构。

branches.en: Long-established power becomes the elite.
branches.cn: 长期稳固的权力变成精英集团。

branches.en: Founding is the first step toward an institution.
branches.cn: 创立是成为机构的第一步。

branches.en: Large institutions make up the establishment.
branches.cn: 大型机构构成权势集团。

intro.en: Establishment adds the noun suffix -ment to establish.
intro.cn: establishment 在 establish 后加名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: Latin stabilis, firm, stands behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stabilis（稳固的）支撑整个词族。

items.exampleCN: established 描述被接受的事物。
anti-establishment 描述对权力的反对。

definition_en: a large area of land with a house, or all the property a person owns
core_image: 一片带大房子的土地，四周是树和围墙
scene: 他祖父留下了一座带花园的老庄园，如今成了当地的景点。His grandfather left an old estate with a garden, which is now a local attraction.
sceneCN: 这里 estate 是「庄园」（第 1 个义项：带房屋的大片乡间土地）；句意：他祖父留下了一座带花园的老庄园，如今成了当地的景点。

senses.title: A large country property
senses.definition: a large area of land in the country with one main house
senses.definitionCN: 乡间带有主屋的大片土地
senses.example: The family has lived on the estate for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家族已在庄园里住了好几代。
senses.why: The Latin source means state or condition, and land held in one state became an estate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为状态，处于同一状态的土地就成为一个庄园。

senses.title: Property and land
senses.definition: land or buildings owned by someone
senses.definitionCN: 某人拥有的土地或建筑
senses.example: He works in real estate in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城里做房地产生意。
senses.why: Property is the modern everyday sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 财产是这个词在现代的日常义项。

senses.title: Property left at death
senses.definition: all the money and property a person leaves when they die
senses.definitionCN: 一个人去世时留下的全部钱财与财产
senses.example: Her estate was divided among three children.
senses.exampleCN: 她的遗产分给了三个孩子。
senses.why: What a person owns at the end of life is their whole estate.
senses.whyCN: 一个人生命结束时拥有的全部财产就是其遗产。

intro.en: Estate comes from Old French estat, from Latin status, a state or condition.
intro.cn: estate 源自古法语 estat，源自拉丁语 status（状态、身份）。

items.en: Status means a state or standing.
Estat means condition or rank.
Estate names the land and position of a family.
items.cn: estate 指家族的土地与地位。

items.en: Estate covers property and inheritance.
items.cn: estate 涵盖房地产与遗产。

items.en: Real estate names land and buildings.
items.cn: real estate 指土地与建筑。

note.en: Estate is close to property and land, and has a special legal sense.
note.cn: estate 与财产、土地相近，并有专门的法律含义。

entries.definition: the solid surface of the earth
property passed down after a death

normalIntro.en: An estate is a whole state of property gathered under one name.
normalIntro.cn: estate 就是一个名字之下聚拢起来的全部财产状态。

normal.en: A country estate is a large house with land.
normal.cn: a country estate 是带土地的乡间大宅。

normal.en: Real estate means land and buildings.
normal.cn: real estate 意为土地与建筑。

normal.en: An estate agent helps people buy property.
normal.cn: estate agent 帮人买房。

normal.en: A person's estate is all they own at death.
normal.cn: 一个人的 estate 是其去世时的全部财产。

normal.en: Compare property: property is any owned thing, an estate is the whole holding.
normal.cn: 对比 property：property 是任何所有物，estate 是全部产业。

abstract.en: Picture a long drive leading to a stone house.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的车道通向石屋。

abstract.en: Imagine a map with one large piece shaded and named.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有一大块被涂色并标名。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed box holding everything a family owns.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的箱子装着一个家庭的全部所有物。

examples.en: The old estate has a huge garden and a lake.
examples.cn: 这座古老庄园有巨大的花园和一个湖。

examples.en: Prices in real estate have risen sharply.
examples.cn: 房地产价格大幅上涨。

examples.en: The estate was divided equally among the heirs.
examples.cn: 遗产在继承人之间平均分配。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estate」听起来像「一块地」——带房子的整片土地，就是庄园或地产；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 status（状态、身份）→ 古法语 estat → estate，核心义「处于同一名下的整片土地与财产」。

sensesIntro.en: Estate first means a large country property, then land and buildings, and finally everything a person leaves at death.
sensesIntro.cn: estate 先指乡间大庄园，再指土地与建筑，最后指去世时留下的全部遗产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled area of land with one large house at its center.
core.cn: 核心意象：围起来的土地上坐落着一栋大房子。

branches.en: A country property is the traditional sense.
branches.cn: 乡间庄园是传统义项。

branches.en: Land and buildings make up modern property.
branches.cn: 土地与建筑构成现代房地产。

branches.en: The whole holding passes on at death.
branches.cn: 全部产业在去世时被传承。

branches.en: An estate is both a home and a piece of property.
branches.cn: 庄园既是家，也是财产。

branches.en: Property owned at death forms the inheritance.
branches.cn: 去世时拥有的财产构成遗产。

intro.en: Estate comes through Old French estat from Latin status, a state.
intro.cn: estate 经古法语 estat 源自拉丁语 status（状态）。

latinIntro.en: Latin status, a standing or condition, gives state, status and estate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 status（身份、状况）衍生出 state、status 与 estate。

items.example: Old French estat carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 estat 传递了该词。

items.example: Real combines with estate for property.
items.exampleCN: real 与 estate 组合指房地产。

items.example: Real estate is a fixed compound.
Agent combines with estate for a broker.
items.exampleCN: agent 与 estate 组合指经纪人。

items.example: Housing combines with estate for a residential area.
items.exampleCN: housing 与 estate 组合指住宅区。

items.example: A housing estate holds many homes.
items.exampleCN: housing estate 包含许多住宅。

definition_en: to guess the size, cost or value of something
core_image: 用眼睛和手比量，给出一串近似的数字
scene: 工程师估计这项工程还需要三个月才能完成。The engineers estimate that the project will need another three months.
sceneCN: 这里 estimate 是「估计」（第 1 个义项：根据现有信息推测数量或时间）；句意：工程师估计这项工程还需要三个月才能完成。

senses.title: Guess an amount
senses.definition: to calculate an amount roughly from available information
senses.definitionCN: 根据现有信息粗略计算数量
senses.example: We estimate the trip will take six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估计这趟行程要六个小时。
senses.why: The Latin source means to value, so estimating puts a number on something uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为估价，因此 estimate 就是给不确定的事物一个数字。

senses.title: Judge worth
senses.definition: to form an opinion about someone's ability or character
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的能力或品格形成看法
senses.example: You should not estimate people by their clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 你不该凭衣着评价人。
senses.why: Valuing a thing and valuing a person use the same act of judgment.
senses.whyCN: 给东西估价与评价一个人，用的是同一种判断行为。

senses.title: A written price
senses.definition: a statement of how much work will cost
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项工作将花费多少钱的单据
senses.example: Ask the builder for an estimate first.
senses.exampleCN: 先向建筑商要一份报价。
senses.why: The noun is the number produced by estimating.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是估计之后得出的数字。

intro.en: Estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value or judge.
intro.cn: estimate 源自拉丁语 aestimare（估价、判断）。

items.en: Aestimare means to value or rate.
Aestimatio means a valuation.
Estimate enters English as a verb and noun.
items.cn: estimate 以动词和名词形式进入英语。

items.en: It covers cost, time and size.
items.cn: 它涵盖成本、时间与规模。

items.en: A written estimate is a common business document.
items.cn: 书面报价是常见的商业文件。

note.en: Estimate is close to calculate and assess, and keeps the idea of value.
note.cn: estimate 与计算、评估相近，并保留「估价」的核心。

entries.definition: to find a number by using math
to judge the quality or value of something
to give an answer without being sure

normalIntro.en: An estimate is a careful guess with a number attached.
normalIntro.cn: estimate 就是附上数字的谨慎猜测。

normal.en: Estimate the cost means work out roughly how much it will be.
normal.cn: estimate the cost 意为粗略算出要花多少钱。

normal.en: A rough estimate is not exact.
normal.cn: a rough estimate 并不精确。

normal.en: It is estimated that introduces a general calculation.
normal.cn: it is estimated that 引出大致的推算。

normal.en: A written estimate can be signed and accepted.
normal.cn: 书面报价可以签字接受。

normal.en: Compare calculate: calculate finds an exact number, estimate finds an approximate one.
normal.cn: 对比 calculate：calculate 求精确数字，estimate 求近似值。

abstract.en: Picture a hand measuring a table by eye.
abstract.cn: 想象用手凭眼力比量一张桌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale that stops between two marks.
abstract.cn: 想象天平停在两个刻度之间。

abstract.en: Think of a number written with a question mark beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字旁边画着问号。

examples.en: Experts estimate the damage at two million.
examples.cn: 专家估计损失为两百万。

examples.en: She is highly estimated by her colleagues.
examples.cn: 她受到同事们的高度评价。

examples.en: The repair shop gave us a free estimate.
examples.cn: 修理店给我们免费报了个价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estimate」读起来像「爱是提么特」——不确定时就先估一个数；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestimare（估价、判断）→ estimate，核心义「给不确定的事物定一个近似价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Estimate first means guess an amount, then judge a person's worth, and as a noun it names a written price.
sensesIntro.cn: estimate 先指估算数量，再指评价人的价值，作名词时指书面报价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number written beside a question mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：问号旁边写下的一个数字。

branches.en: Roughly calculating an amount is the main sense.
branches.cn: 粗略计算数量是主要义项。

branches.en: Judging worth uses the same valuing act.
branches.cn: 评价价值用的是同一种估价行为。

branches.en: The noun is the price on paper.
branches.cn: 名词指纸面上的报价。

branches.en: A written estimate records a calculation.
branches.cn: 书面报价记录了一次估算。

branches.en: Estimating numbers and estimating people both require judgment.
branches.cn: 估算数字与评价人都需要判断。

intro.en: Estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value, with the noun suffix -ate.
intro.cn: estimate 源自拉丁语 aestimare（估价），带名词性词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestimare means to value or rate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare 意为估价或评定。

items.example: Estimate is both verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: estimate 既是动词也是名词。
词尾 -ate 塑造动词形式。

items.example: Overestimate means set the number too high.
items.exampleCN: overestimate 意为把数字估得过高。

items.example: Underestimate means set the number too low.
items.exampleCN: underestimate 意为把数字估得过低。

definition_zh: 民族的；种族的；民族风情的
definition_en: relating to a group of people with a shared culture or origin
core_image: 一群人穿着相同的传统服饰，围在一起唱歌
scene: 这个街区住着许多不同民族的家庭，节日时格外热闹。This neighborhood is home to families of many ethnic groups, and it becomes lively during festivals.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnic 是「民族的」（第 1 个义项：与共享文化或血统的群体有关）；句意：这个街区住着许多不同民族的家庭，节日时格外热闹。

pos.zh: 民族的；种族的；民族风情的

senses.title: Relating to a people
senses.definition: connected with a group that shares culture, language or origin
senses.definitionCN: 与共享文化、语言或血统的群体有关
senses.example: The city has many ethnic communities.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有许多族群社区。
senses.why: The Greek source means nation or people, so ethnic marks what belongs to a people.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为民族或人民，因此 ethnic 标记属于某个民族的事物。

senses.title: Traditional cultural style
senses.definition: in a traditional style of a particular people
senses.definitionCN: 采用某一民族的传统风格
senses.example: She wore an ethnic dress to the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件民族风连衣裙去参加节日。
senses.why: Culture shows in clothing and design, so ethnic also describes that style.
senses.whyCN: 文化体现在服饰与设计中，因此 ethnic 也描述这种风格。

intro.en: Ethnic comes from Greek ethnos, a nation or people, through Latin ethnicus.
intro.cn: ethnic 经拉丁语 ethnicus 源自希腊语 ethnos（民族、人民）。

items.en: Ethnos means a nation or people.
Ethnikos means belonging to a people.
items.cn: ethnikos 意为属于某个民族的。

items.en: Ethnicus carries the word into Latin.
Ethnic describes peoples and their cultures.
items.cn: ethnic 描述民族及其文化。

items.en: It also describes traditional styles.

note.en: Ethnic is close to racial and cultural, but focuses on a people and its culture.
note.cn: ethnic 与种族的、文化的相近，但侧重民族及其文化。

normalIntro.en: Ethnic points to a people: its language, food and festivals.
normalIntro.cn: ethnic 指向一个民族：它的语言、食物与节日。

normal.en: An ethnic group shares a culture.
normal.cn: ethnic group 共享一种文化。

normal.en: An ethnic minority is a smaller people within a country.
normal.cn: ethnic minority 指一国之内人数较少的民族。

normal.en: Ethnic food comes from a particular tradition.
normal.cn: ethnic food 来自特定传统。

normal.en: Ethnic identity is the sense of belonging to a people.
normal.cn: ethnic identity 是归属于某民族的意识。

normal.en: Compare ethic: ethic is about morals, ethnic is about peoples.
normal.cn: 对比 ethic：ethic 关乎道德，ethnic 关乎民族。

abstract.en: Picture a table full of dishes from one tradition.
abstract.cn: 想象一桌来自同一传统的菜肴。

abstract.en: Imagine a song sung in a language you do not know.
abstract.cn: 想象一首用陌生语言唱的歌。

abstract.en: Think of a pattern woven the same way for generations.
abstract.cn: 想象一个世代相传的编织花纹。

examples.en: The school welcomes students from many ethnic backgrounds.
examples.cn: 学校欢迎来自许多民族背景的学生。

examples.en: The market sells ethnic food from around the world.
examples.cn: 市场上出售来自世界各地的民族风味食物。

examples.en: She studies ethnic music of the region.
examples.cn: 她研究该地区的民族音乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ethnic」听起来像「爱死尼克」——每个民族都有自己的特色，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ethnos（民族、人民）→ ethnikos（民族的）→ 拉丁语 ethnicus → ethnic，核心义「属于某个民族及其文化」。

sensesIntro.en: Ethnic first describes peoples and their shared culture, and then the traditional style that comes from that culture.
sensesIntro.cn: ethnic 先描述民族及其共享文化，再描述由该文化而来的传统风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people in traditional dress singing together.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿着传统服饰的人们一起唱歌。

branches.en: The first sense links a person to a people.
branches.cn: 首要义项把人与其民族联系起来。

branches.en: The second sense describes traditional style.
branches.cn: 第二个义项描述传统风格。

branches.en: Culture shapes the clothing and food people call ethnic.
branches.cn: 文化塑造了人们称为民族风情的服饰与食物。

branches.en: Ethnic identity is a common modern phrase.
branches.cn: ethnic identity 是常见的现代短语。

branches.en: Ethnic design borrows patterns from a tradition.
branches.cn: 民族风格的设计借用传统花纹。

intro.en: Ethnic comes from Greek ethnos, people, with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: ethnic 源自希腊语 ethnos（人民），带形容词词尾 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Latin ethnicus borrowed the Greek word before English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ethnicus 先借入这个希腊词，再传入英语。

items.example: Ethnicus carries the word to Latin.

definition_zh: 甚至；连……都；平坦的；均匀的；偶数的
definition_en: used to stress something surprising, or describing something flat, regular or equal
core_image: 一条完全水平的地面，无论怎么走都没有高低起伏
scene: 他忙了一整天，甚至连午饭都忘了吃。He was busy all day and even forgot to eat lunch.
sceneCN: 这里 even 是「甚至」（第 1 个义项：用来强调出人意料的情况）；句意：他忙了一整天，甚至连午饭都忘了吃。

senses.title: Used for emphasis
senses.definition: used to stress something that is surprising or extreme
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调令人意外或极端的情况
senses.example: He even brought flowers to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他甚至带花来开会。
senses.why: The emphatic use grows from the idea of equality: this case is as true as the others.
senses.whyCN: 强调用法来自「同等」的观念：这种情况与其余情况一样真实。

senses.title: Flat and level
senses.definition: flat and level, with no higher or lower parts
senses.definitionCN: 平坦水平，没有高低起伏
senses.example: The table has an even surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌面很平。
senses.why: The oldest sense is level, where every point has the same height.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是水平，即每一点高度相同。

senses.title: Regular and equal
senses.definition: regular, equal or balanced in amount or spacing
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或间隔上规则、相等或均衡
senses.example: Spread the paint in an even layer.
senses.exampleCN: 把颜料涂成均匀的一层。
senses.why: Equal height becomes equal amount when applied more widely.
senses.whyCN: 把「等高的」扩展到更广范围，就是「等量的」。

senses.title: Divisible by two
senses.definition: a number that can be divided by two exactly
senses.definitionCN: 能被二整除的数
senses.example: Two, four and six are even numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 二、四、六都是偶数。
senses.why: An even number splits into two equal halves, matching the idea of balance.
senses.whyCN: 偶数能分成两个相等的半，符合均衡的观念。

senses.title: Make equal
senses.definition: to make something equal or level
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物相等或平坦
senses.example: The final goal evened the score.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个进球把比分扳平了。
senses.why: The verb turns the adjective into the act of making things level.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「平的」变成「使变平」的动作。

intro.en: Even comes from Old English efen, meaning level or equal.
intro.cn: even 源自古英语 efen（平的、相等的）。

items.en: Efen means level or equal.
Even describes flat ground and equal shares.
items.cn: even 描述平地与均等的份额。

items.en: The word also names numbers divisible by two.
items.cn: 这个词也指能被二整除的数。

items.en: As an adverb it adds emphasis.
Even though and even if mark contrast.
items.cn: even though 与 even if 标记让步对比。

note.en: Even is a common word with level, equal and emphatic uses.
note.cn: even 是常用词，兼有平坦、相等与强调的用法。

entries.definition: the same in size or amount

normalIntro.en: Even begins with a level line: flat ground, equal shares, balanced numbers.
normalIntro.cn: even 从一条水平线开始：平地、均分、平衡的数字。

normal.en: Even though introduces a fact that does not change the result.
normal.cn: even though 引出一个不改变结果的事实。

normal.en: Even if imagines a case that may not happen.
normal.cn: even if 想象一种可能不发生的假设。

normal.en: An even surface has no bumps.
normal.cn: an even surface 没有凸起。

normal.en: An even number divides into two equal parts.
normal.cn: 偶数能分成两个相等的部分。

normal.en: Compare level: level stresses height, even stresses lack of variation.
normal.cn: 对比 level：level 强调高度，even 强调没有变化。

abstract.en: Picture a calm lake with no waves.
abstract.cn: 想象一片没有波浪的平静湖面。

abstract.en: Imagine a rope pulled straight and taut.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被拉得笔直紧绷的绳子。

abstract.en: Think of two children sharing a cake equally.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子平均分一块蛋糕。

examples.en: She even forgot her own birthday.
examples.cn: 她甚至忘了自己的生日。

examples.en: The ground is not even enough for a tent.
examples.cn: 地面不够平，搭不了帐篷。

examples.en: Cut the bread into even slices.
examples.cn: 把面包切成厚度均匀的片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「even」有「一平」的感觉——平平整整、不多不少，于是也有「甚至」的强调；这只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 efen（平的、相等的）→ even，核心义「没有高低差别、彼此相等」。

sensesIntro.en: Even starts with emphasis, then describes flat surfaces, regular amounts, numbers split in two, and the act of making things equal.
sensesIntro.cn: even 从强调用法开始，再指平坦表面、均匀数量、可对分的数字，以及使事物相等的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a perfectly level line with no bumps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条完全没有起伏的水平线。

branches.en: The adverb adds surprising emphasis.
branches.cn: 副词增加出人意料的强调。

branches.en: A flat surface has the same height throughout.
branches.cn: 平坦表面处处同高。

branches.en: Regular spacing and amount extend the flat idea.
branches.cn: 规则的间隔与数量延伸了「平」的概念。

branches.en: Even numbers split into two equal halves.
branches.cn: 偶数能分成两个相等的半。

branches.en: The verb makes a score or surface level.
branches.cn: 动词使比分或表面变平。

intro.en: Even is a native Old English word and takes suffixes such as -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: even 是古英语本族词，可加 -ly、-ness 等后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Though combines with even to mark contrast.
items.exampleCN: though 与 even 组合表示让步对比。

items.example: If combines with even for a hypothetical case.
items.exampleCN: if 与 even 组合表示假设情况。

definition_en: the part of the day between afternoon and night
core_image: 太阳落山后，窗户里一盏盏灯亮起来
scene: 傍晚时分，湖面映着落日，安静得像一面镜子。In the evening, the lake reflected the setting sun and was as quiet as a mirror.
sceneCN: 这里 evening 是「傍晚」（第 1 个义项：下午与夜晚之间的时段）；句意：傍晚时分，湖面映着落日，安静得像一面镜子。

senses.title: The end of the day
senses.definition: the time between the afternoon and night
senses.definitionCN: 下午与夜晚之间的时间
senses.example: We usually take a walk in the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 我们通常在傍晚散步。
senses.why: The word comes from an Old English word for the time when light fades.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古英语中表示光线渐暗时段的词。

senses.title: An evening event
senses.definition: an event or party that happens in the evening
senses.definitionCN: 在晚上举行的活动或聚会
senses.example: The school held a musical evening.
senses.exampleCN: 学校举办了一场音乐晚会。
senses.why: A gathering named by its time of day becomes the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 以时段命名的聚会，最终就指这个活动本身。

intro.en: Evening comes from Old English ǣfnung, the coming of evening, from ǣfen.
intro.cn: evening 源自古英语 ǣfnung（傍晚的到来），来自 ǣfen。

items.en: Ǣfen means evening.
Ǣfnung means the coming of evening.
Evening settles into its modern shape.
items.cn: evening 逐渐固定为现代词形。

items.en: Evening also names social events.
Good evening is a standard greeting.
items.cn: good evening 是标准问候语。

note.en: Evening is close to night and dusk, and shorter than the whole night.
note.cn: evening 与夜晚、黄昏相近，但短于整个夜晚。

entries.definition: the time when day becomes night
the dark part of the day

normalIntro.en: Evening is when lamps go on and the day begins to close.
normalIntro.cn: evening 就是灯亮起来、一天开始收尾的时候。

normal.en: In the evening means after the afternoon.
normal.cn: in the evening 意为下午之后。

normal.en: Good evening is said after about six.
normal.cn: good evening 大约在六点以后使用。

normal.en: An evening class meets at night.
normal.cn: evening class 在晚上上课。

normal.en: A musical evening is a concert in the evening.
normal.cn: a musical evening 是晚间音乐会。

normal.en: Compare night: evening ends when you go to bed, night lasts until morning.
normal.cn: 对比 night：evening 到你睡觉为止，night 持续到早晨。

abstract.en: Picture windows lighting up one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇窗户依次亮起。

abstract.en: Imagine a table set for dinner under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下摆好晚餐的桌子。

abstract.en: Think of a sky turning from gold to deep blue.
abstract.cn: 想象天空从金色变成深蓝。

examples.en: The museum is open until late in the evening.
examples.cn: 博物馆开放到深夜。

examples.en: We spent the evening talking by the fire.
examples.cn: 我们在火边聊了一晚上。

examples.en: She teaches an evening class twice a week.
examples.cn: 她每周上两次夜间课程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「even（平）＋ ing」——天色渐渐变平、暗下来，就是傍晚；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ǣfen（傍晚）→ ǣfnung（傍晚的到来）→ evening，核心义「白天与夜晚之间的时段」。

sensesIntro.en: Evening first names the end of the day, and then the gatherings held at that time.
sensesIntro.cn: evening 先指一天的尾段，再指在这个时段举行的聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: windows lighting up after the sun goes down.
core.cn: 核心意象：日落之后一扇扇亮起的窗。

branches.en: The time of day is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 一天中的时段是基本义。

branches.en: An event at that time takes the same name.
branches.cn: 在该时段举行的活动也取同一名称。

branches.en: The time and the party share one word.
branches.cn: 时段与聚会共用一个词。

branches.en: Greetings mark the start of the evening.
branches.cn: 问候语标记傍晚的开始。

branches.en: Concerts and classes fill the evening.
branches.cn: 音乐会和课程填满夜晚。

intro.en: Evening is a native word formed from an Old English root plus -ing.
intro.cn: evening 是由古英语词根加 -ing 构成的本族词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Ǣfnung is the older form of evening.
items.exampleCN: ǣfnung 是 evening 的较早形式。

items.example: Evenings can act as an adverb.

definition_en: something that happens, especially something important or planned
core_image: 日历上的一个圆圈，把某一天紧紧标了出来
scene: 这场音乐节是城里一年中最大的文化活动。This music festival is the city's biggest cultural event of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 event 是「活动」（第 2 个义项：有组织、按计划举行的场合）；句意：这场音乐节是城里一年中最大的文化活动。

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: something that happens, especially something important
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事情，尤其是重要的事
senses.example: The discovery was a major event in science.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现是科学界的重大事件。
senses.why: The Latin source means an outcome, so an event is what comes out of a situation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为结果，因此事件就是从某种情况中产生的事。

senses.title: A planned occasion
senses.definition: an organized occasion such as a party or festival
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的场合，如聚会或节日庆典
senses.example: The charity holds a fund-raising event each year.
senses.exampleCN: 该慈善机构每年举办一次筹款活动。
senses.why: An occasion planned in advance is an event on the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 提前计划的场合就是日历上的一件活动。

senses.title: A sports contest
senses.definition: one of the races or competitions in a sports meeting
senses.definitionCN: 运动会中的一项比赛
senses.example: The long jump is her best event.
senses.exampleCN: 跳远是她最擅长的项目。
senses.why: A single contest is one scheduled happening within a larger meeting.
senses.whyCN: 单项比赛是大型运动会中安排的一次具体发生。

intro.en: Event comes from Latin eventus, an outcome, from evenire, to come out.
intro.cn: event 源自拉丁语 eventus（结果），来自 evenire（出来、发生）。

items.en: Evenire means to come out or happen.
Eventus means an outcome.
Evenement means something that happens.
Event covers important happenings.
It also names planned occasions and contests.
items.cn: 它也指计划好的活动与比赛。

note.en: Event is close to incident and occasion, and is broader than either.
note.cn: event 与事件、场合相近，但比两者都宽泛。

normalIntro.en: An event is a date circled on the calendar: something happens there.
normalIntro.cn: event 就是日历上被圈出的日子：那天有事情发生。

normal.en: A major event is important enough to remember.
normal.cn: major event 重要到值得记住。

normal.en: A sporting event draws a crowd.
normal.cn: sporting event 会吸引人群。

normal.en: In the event of rain means if rain happens.
normal.cn: in the event of rain 意为如果下雨。

normal.en: Current events are recent news happenings.
normal.cn: current events 是近期新闻事件。

normal.en: Compare incident: an incident is usually small or unpleasant, an event can be planned.
normal.cn: 对比 incident：incident 通常较小或不愉快，event 可以是计划好的。

abstract.en: Picture one day on a calendar circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上有一天被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Imagine a stage waiting for a crowd to arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台等待人群到来。

abstract.en: Think of a page of news filled with big headlines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页写满大标题的新闻。

examples.en: The wedding was the biggest event of the year.
examples.cn: 婚礼是那一年最大的事件。

examples.en: She helped organize a charity event.
examples.cn: 她帮忙组织了一场慈善活动。

examples.en: The team won three events at the games.
examples.cn: 该队在运动会上赢得了三个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「event」听起来像「一万一」——值得记下的大事；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 e-（出）＋ venire（来）→ evenire（发生）→ eventus（结果）→ event，核心义「从情况中产生、发生的事情」。

sensesIntro.en: Event first names anything that happens, then a planned occasion, and finally one contest in a sports meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: event 先指发生的任何事，再指计划好的场合，最后指运动会中的单项比赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a day circled on a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被圈出的一天。

branches.en: Anything important that happens is an event.
branches.cn: 发生的任何重要事情都是事件。

branches.en: Planned occasions are events on a schedule.
branches.cn: 计划好的场合是日程上的活动。

branches.en: One contest is an event within a meeting.
branches.cn: 单项比赛是运动会中的一项赛事。

branches.en: A planned event becomes a remembered happening.
branches.cn: 计划好的活动会成为被记住的事件。

branches.en: Sports meetings are events made of events.
branches.cn: 运动会是由多项赛事组成的活动。

intro.en: Event comes from Latin evenire, to come out, with the noun ending -tus.
intro.cn: event 源自拉丁语 evenire（出来、发生），带名词词尾 -tus。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire, to come, gives event, prevent and invent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire（来）衍生出 event、prevent 与 invent。

items.exampleCN: eventful 描述忙碌多事的时期。

definition_en: in the end, especially after a long time or many difficulties
core_image: 一条长长的路终于走到尽头，前方出现一扇门
scene: 经过多次失败，他终于找到了正确的方法。After many failures, he eventually found the right method.
sceneCN: 这里 eventually 是「最终」（第 1 个义项：经历一段时间或困难之后终于如此）；句意：经过多次失败，他终于找到了正确的方法。

senses.title: In the end
senses.definition: at the end of a long process or period
senses.definitionCN: 在漫长过程或时期的末尾
senses.example: The train eventually arrived two hours late.
senses.exampleCN: 火车最终晚点两小时到达。
senses.why: The word comes from event, so it points to the outcome that finally comes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 event，因此指向最终到来的结果。

senses.title: As a final outcome
senses.definition: used to describe what happens as the final result
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明作为最终结果而发生的事
senses.example: The delay eventually cost them the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误最终让他们失去了合同。
senses.why: Eventual describes the last outcome, and the adverb points to that end point.
senses.whyCN: eventual 描述最后的结果，副词则指向那个终点。

intro.en: Eventually is eventual plus -ly, from Latin eventus, an outcome.
intro.cn: eventually 是 eventual 加 -ly，源自拉丁语 eventus（结果）。

items.en: Eventus means an outcome.
Eventual means happening at the end.
The adverb eventually marks the end of a process.
items.cn: 副词 eventually 标记过程的终点。

items.en: It often suggests delay or difficulty.
Eventually is common in narrative and reports.
items.cn: eventually 常见于叙事与报告中。

note.en: Eventually is close to finally and in the end, with a sense of long delay.
note.cn: eventually 与 finally、in the end 相近，带有长期拖延的意味。

normalIntro.en: Eventually marks the door at the end of a very long corridor.
normalIntro.cn: eventually 标记着漫长走廊尽头的那扇门。

normal.en: Eventually become means become so after time.
normal.cn: eventually become 意为经过时间之后成为。

normal.en: Eventually lead to means cause in the end.
normal.cn: eventually lead to 意为最终导致。

normal.en: Eventually agree means agree after long talks.
normal.cn: eventually agree 意为长时间商谈后同意。

normal.en: Sooner or later is a close everyday phrase.
normal.cn: sooner or later 是意思接近的日常短语。

normal.en: Compare finally: finally can mark the last item, eventually stresses the long wait.
normal.cn: 对比 finally：finally 可标记最后一项，eventually 强调漫长等待。

abstract.en: Picture a train that is late but still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一列晚点却终究到站的火车。

abstract.en: Imagine a seed that grows after a long winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子在漫长冬天后发芽。

abstract.en: Think of a page turned after many chapters.
abstract.cn: 想象翻过许多章节之后终于翻到的一页。

examples.en: She eventually agreed to help us.
examples.cn: 她最终同意帮助我们。

examples.en: The plan eventually failed.
examples.cn: 这个计划最终失败了。

examples.en: They eventually moved to a smaller house.
examples.cn: 他们最终搬进了一所较小的房子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「event（事件）＋ ually」——所有事件走到最后，就是最终；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 eventus（结果）→ eventual（最终的）＋ -ly → eventually，核心义「经过漫长过程后到达结果」。

sensesIntro.en: Eventually first means in the end after a long time, and then describes the final outcome itself.
sensesIntro.cn: eventually 先指经过漫长时间后终于如此，再描述最终的结局本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door at the far end of a long corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：漫长走廊尽头的一扇门。

branches.en: The main sense is reaching the end at last.
branches.cn: 主要义项是终于到达终点。

branches.en: The word can also label the final result.
branches.cn: 这个词也能标记最终结果。

branches.en: The long wait and the final outcome belong together.
branches.cn: 漫长等待与最终结果彼此相连。

branches.en: Delay is often implied but not required.
branches.cn: 延误常被暗示，但并非必需。

branches.en: Reports use the word to close a sequence.
branches.cn: 报告用这个词收束一系列事件。

intro.en: Eventually is eventual plus -ly, with event at the root.
intro.cn: eventually 是 eventual 加 -ly，词根是 event。

latinIntro.en: Latin eventus, an outcome, gives event and eventually.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 eventus（结果）衍生出 event 与 eventually。

definition_en: at any time, or used to give emphasis to a question
core_image: 一条延伸到无限远的时间线，任何一点都被覆盖
scene: 你曾经见过这么美的星空吗？Have you ever seen such a beautiful starry sky?
sceneCN: 这里 ever 是「曾经」（第 1 个义项：在过去的任何时间）；句意：你曾经见过这么美的星空吗？

senses.title: At any time
senses.definition: at any time in the past, present or future
senses.definitionCN: 在过去、现在或未来的任何时间
senses.example: Nothing like this has ever happened before.
senses.exampleCN: 以前从未发生过这样的事。
senses.why: The Old English source means at any time, which is still the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语来源意为「在任何时候」，这仍是核心含义。

senses.title: Emphasis in questions
senses.definition: used to stress surprise or annoyance in a question
senses.definitionCN: 在疑问句中强调惊讶或不满
senses.example: Why would she ever agree to that?
senses.exampleCN: 她究竟为什么会同意那种事？
senses.why: Any time becomes any possible case, which strengthens the question.
senses.whyCN: 「任何时间」变成「任何可能的情况」，从而加强疑问。

senses.title: Continuously
senses.definition: always or continuously, used in compounds
senses.definitionCN: 始终或不断地，用于复合词
senses.example: The ever-changing city never feels the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这座不断变化的城市从不让人有相同的感觉。
senses.why: Extending through all times produces the sense of constant change.
senses.whyCN: 贯穿所有时间，就产生了「持续不断」的含义。

intro.en: Ever comes from Old English ǣfre, meaning at any time.
intro.cn: ever 源自古英语 ǣfre（在任何时候）。

items.en: Ǣfre means at any time.
Ǣfre lc means ever each, the source of every.
items.cn: ǣfre ǣlc 意为每一个，是 every 的来源。

items.en: Ever appears in questions and comparisons.
items.cn: ever 出现在疑问与比较中。

items.en: Ever since marks a starting point.
Ever combines with participles for constant action.
items.cn: ever 与分词组合表示持续动作。

note.en: Ever is close to always and at any time, but usually needs a question or negative.
note.cn: ever 与 always、在任何时候相近，但通常用于疑问或否定。

normalIntro.en: Ever stretches across all times, so it often needs a question to make sense.
normalIntro.cn: ever 横跨所有时间，因此常需要疑问句来落实含义。

normal.en: Have you ever asks about any past time.
normal.cn: have you ever 询问过去任何时候。

normal.en: Ever since means from that time until now.
normal.cn: ever since 意为从那时直到现在。

normal.en: Hardly ever means almost never.
normal.cn: hardly ever 意为几乎从不。

normal.en: As ever means as always.
normal.cn: as ever 意为一如既往。

normal.en: Compare always: always states all times, ever asks about any time.
normal.cn: 对比 always：always 陈述所有时间，ever 询问任何时间。

abstract.en: Picture a line that runs past the horizon in both directions.
abstract.cn: 想象一条向两端延伸、越过地平线的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock with no beginning and no end.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没有起点也没有终点的钟。

abstract.en: Think of a door that opens at every hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇每个整点都会打开的门。

examples.en: Have you ever tried rock climbing?
examples.cn: 你曾经尝试过攀岩吗？

examples.en: It was the best film I had ever seen.
examples.cn: 那是我看过的最好的电影。

examples.en: She is as cheerful as ever.
examples.cn: 她一如既往地开朗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ever」听起来像「哎我」——回想过去某时曾做过什么；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ǣfre（在任何时候）→ ever，核心义「时间线上的任意一点」。

sensesIntro.en: Ever first covers any time at all, then strengthens a surprised question, and finally marks constant action.
sensesIntro.cn: ever 先覆盖任何时间，再加强惊讶的疑问，最后标记持续不断的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a timeline stretching past both horizons.
core.cn: 核心意象：向两端地平线延伸的时间线。

branches.en: Any time at all is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 任何时间就是基本义。

branches.en: Questions use the word for surprise.
branches.cn: 疑问句用这个词表达惊讶。

branches.en: Compounds extend it to constant action.
branches.cn: 复合词把它延伸到持续动作。

branches.en: Asking if something ever happened stresses how unlikely it seems.
branches.cn: 询问某事是否曾经发生，强调其多么不可能。

branches.en: All times together produce the sense of always.
branches.cn: 所有时间合在一起就产生「总是」的含义。

intro.en: Ever is a native Old English word and often combines with other words.
intro.cn: ever 是古英语本族词，常与其他词组合。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源。

items.exampleCN: never 由 n 与 ever 组合。
every 由 ever each 演变而来。
evermore 由 ever 与 more 组成。

items.example: Since combines with ever for a starting point.
items.exampleCN: since 与 ever 组合表示起点。

items.example: Hardly combines with ever for almost never.
items.exampleCN: hardly 与 ever 组合表示几乎从不。

definition_zh: 每一个；所有可能的；每隔
definition_en: each one of a group, or each interval of time or distance
core_image: 一排一模一样的格子，从左到右逐个被点亮
scene: 她每天早晨都会绕着公园跑一圈。She runs around the park every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 every 是「每一个」（第 1 个义项：指群体中的每一个成员或每一次）；句意：她每天早晨都会绕着公园跑一圈。

pos.zh: 每一个；所有可能的；每隔

senses.title: Each one
senses.definition: each member of a group, considered one by one
senses.definitionCN: 群体中的每个成员，逐个看待
senses.example: Every student received a new book.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都领到了一本新书。
senses.why: The word grew from ever each, meaning each one without exception.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 ever each 演变而来，意为毫无例外的每一个。

senses.title: All possible
senses.definition: used to show that all possible examples are included
senses.definitionCN: 用于表明包含所有可能的例子
senses.example: She showed every kindness to her guests.
senses.exampleCN: 她对客人表现出了种种善意。
senses.why: Each one without exception can widen into every kind.
senses.whyCN: 毫无例外的每一个，可以扩展为每一种。

senses.title: At regular intervals
senses.definition: used before a number to mean at each interval
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字前，表示每隔一段时间或距离
senses.example: The bus comes every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 公共汽车每十分钟来一班。
senses.why: Repeating each unit creates an interval, one after another.
senses.whyCN: 每个单位重复一次，就形成一段接一段的间隔。

intro.en: Every comes from Old English ǣfre ǣlc, ever each.
intro.cn: every 源自古英语 ǣfre ǣlc（ever each，每一个）。

items.en: Ǣfre means ever.
Ǣlc means each.
Ǣfre ǣlc means each one without exception.
items.cn: ǣfre ǣlc 意为毫无例外的每一个。

items.en: The two words merge into every.
Every also marks regular intervals.
items.cn: every 也标记规律的间隔。

note.en: Every is close to each and all, but treats a group one by one.
note.cn: every 与 each、all 相近，但把群体逐个看待。

normalIntro.en: Every joins ever and each: every single one, without missing any.
normalIntro.cn: every 由 ever 与 each 组成：每一个都不漏。

normal.en: Every day means each day in a row.
normal.cn: every day 意为一天接一天。

normal.en: Every one of means not a single exception.
normal.cn: every one of 意为没有一个例外。

normal.en: Every other day means one day on, one day off.
normal.cn: every other day 意为隔一天。

normal.en: Every now and then means from time to time.
normal.cn: every now and then 意为不时地。

normal.en: Compare each: each stresses separate items, every stresses the whole group.
normal.cn: 对比 each：each 强调分开的个体，every 强调整个群体。

abstract.en: Picture identical boxes opened one after another.
abstract.cn: 想象一模一样的盒子一个接一个被打开。

abstract.en: Imagine footprints covering a whole beach.
abstract.cn: 想象脚印铺满整片沙滩。

abstract.en: Think of a clock striking each hour without fail.
abstract.cn: 想象时钟每个整点都准确敲响。

examples.en: Every room has a window.
examples.cn: 每个房间都有一扇窗。

examples.en: He gave me every reason to trust him.
examples.cn: 他给了我种种信任他的理由。

examples.en: The train leaves every hour.
examples.cn: 火车每小时开一班。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ever（任何时候）＋ y」——任何一次都算上，就是每一个；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ǣfre ǣlc（任何时候的每一个）→ every，核心义「逐个覆盖、一个不漏」。

sensesIntro.en: Every first means each one in a group, then all possible kinds, and finally each regular interval.
sensesIntro.cn: every 先指群体中的每一个，再指所有可能的种类，最后指每个规律间隔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: identical slots lit up one after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一模一样的格子被逐个点亮。

branches.en: Each member in turn is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 逐个成员是基本义。

branches.en: The word can widen to all possible examples.
branches.cn: 这个词能扩展到所有可能的例子。

branches.en: Repeated units create regular intervals.
branches.cn: 重复的单位形成规律间隔。

branches.en: Every member and every kind share the idea of no exception.
branches.cn: 每个成员与每种类型共享「无例外」的观念。

branches.en: The same unit repeated becomes an interval.
branches.cn: 同一个单位重复就形成间隔。

intro.en: Every is a native compound of ever and each, now written as one word.
intro.cn: every 是 ever 与 each 的本族复合词，如今写成一个词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Every combines the two old words.
One combines with every for everyone.
items.exampleCN: one 与 every 组合成 everyone。

items.example: Thing combines with every for everything.
items.exampleCN: thing 与 every 组合成 everything。

items.example: Where combines with every for everywhere.
items.exampleCN: where 与 every 组合成 everywhere。

items.example: Day combines with every for everyday.
items.exampleCN: day 与 every 组合成 everyday。

items.example: Body combines with every for everybody.
items.exampleCN: body 与 every 组合成 everybody。

definition_en: every person
core_image: 操场上一张张朝向主席台的脸
scene: 铃响之后，全校每个人都站到操场上。When the bell rang, everybody in the school stood on the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 everybody 是「每个人、大家」（第 1 个义项：在场的所有人）；句意：铃响之后，全校每个人都站到操场上。

senses.title: All people present
senses.definition: every person in a group or place
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体或场所中的每一个人
senses.example: Everybody was ready to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都准备好出发了。
senses.why: Every and body join to mean every person.
senses.whyCN: every 与 body 结合，表示每一个人。

senses.title: People in general
senses.definition: people in general, including the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 泛指包括说话者在内的众人
senses.example: Everybody knows the story.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都知道这个故事。
senses.why: The word can address a whole community.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指整个群体。

senses.title: An informal address
senses.definition: used to speak to a whole group
senses.definitionCN: 用于向一整群人说话
senses.example: Everybody, please sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 各位，请坐下。
senses.why: The word can open a speech or announcement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以用于演讲或通知的开头。

intro.en: Everybody joins every to body, an old word for a person.
intro.cn: everybody 由 every 与 body（古义为人的身体）组合而成。

items.en: Bodig means a body or a person.
Every means each one of a group.
items.cn: every 意为群体中的每一个。

items.en: Every plus body forms everybody.
items.cn: every 加 body 构成 everybody。

items.en: It means every person.
It is common in everyday speech.
items.cn: 它在日常口语中很常用。

note.en: Everybody is informal and takes a singular verb.
note.cn: everybody 较口语化，语法上接单数动词。

normalIntro.en: Everybody is every body gathered into one word.
normalIntro.cn: everybody 就是每一个身体聚成一个词。

definition_en: every person

senses.title: Every person

note.en: Everyone and everybody mean the same, but everyone is commoner in writing.

normalIntro.en: Everyone is every one person standing together.

normal.en: Everyone here means all people in this place.

normal.en: Everyone knows means it is common knowledge.

normal.en: Thank everyone means thank all of them.

normal.en: Compare everybody: same meaning, more informal.

abstract.en: Think of a light that reaches every corner at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一束同时照到每个角落的光。

examples.en: Everyone needs someone to talk to.
examples.cn: 每个人都需要一个可以说话的人。

examples.en: Everyone agreed with her plan.

items.example: One means a single person here.

items.example: An is the old form of one.

definition_zh: 每件事；一切；最重要的事
definition_en: all things
core_image: 搬家时堆满房间的纸箱，标签写满各种物品名
scene: 搬家那天，屋里的一切都被装进纸箱。On moving day, everything in the house was packed into boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 everything 是「一切事物」（第 1 个义项：某一情境中的所有事物）；句意：搬家那天，屋里的一切都被装进纸箱。

pos.zh: 每件事；一切；最重要的事

senses.title: All things
senses.definition: all things in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 某一情境中的所有事物
senses.example: Everything in the room was new.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里的一切都是新的。
senses.why: Every and thing join to cover all objects.
senses.whyCN: every 与 thing 结合，涵盖所有事物。

senses.title: All that matters
senses.definition: the thing of greatest importance
senses.definitionCN: 最重要的事情
senses.example: Her family is everything to her.
senses.exampleCN: 家人对她来说就是一切。
senses.why: The word can carry emotional weight beyond objects.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能承载超出物品的情感重量。

senses.title: All details
senses.definition: all the details of a matter
senses.definitionCN: 一件事的所有细节
senses.example: Tell me everything about the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 把旅行的所有细节都告诉我。
senses.why: The same word covers the full set of facts.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也涵盖全部事实。

intro.en: Everything joins every to thing, an old word for an object or matter.
intro.cn: everything 由 every 与 thing（古义为物品或事情）组合而成。

items.en: Thing means an object or matter.
Every means each member of a set.
items.cn: every 意为集合中的每一个。

items.en: Every plus thing forms everything.
items.cn: every 加 thing 构成 everything。

items.en: It means all objects in a situation.
items.cn: 它指某一情境中的所有物品。

items.en: It can also mean what matters most.
items.cn: 它也可以指最重要的事。

note.en: Everything covers all things; something is one unknown thing.
note.cn: everything 涵盖所有事物；something 指某件未知的事。

normalIntro.en: Everything is every thing packed into one word.
normalIntro.cn: everything 就是每一件东西装进一个词。

normal.en: Everything else means all the other things.
normal.cn: everything else 意为其他一切。

normal.en: Lose everything means lose all you have.
normal.cn: lose everything 意为失去所有。

normal.en: Everything in order means all is ready.
normal.cn: everything in order 意为一切就绪。

normal.en: Tell me everything means tell all details.
normal.cn: tell me everything 意为告诉我所有细节。

normal.en: Compare nothing: everything is all, nothing is none.
normal.cn: 对比 nothing：everything 是全部，nothing 是什么都没有。

abstract.en: Picture boxes filling a room, each with a label.
abstract.cn: 想象纸箱堆满房间，每只都贴着标签。

abstract.en: Imagine a net that catches every floating object.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网兜住每一件漂浮之物。

abstract.en: Think of a word that leaves nothing outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不把任何东西排除在外的词。

examples.en: Everything was ready before the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 客人到达前一切都准备好了。

examples.en: She told me everything about her new job.
examples.cn: 她把新工作的所有情况都告诉我了。

examples.en: His music means everything to him.
examples.cn: 音乐对他来说意味着一切。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「every（每个）＋ thing（东西）」——每一件东西，就是一切。

root: every（每个）＋ thing（物品、事情）→ everything，核心义「所有事物」。

sensesIntro.en: Everything names all objects, then what matters most, and finally the full set of details.
sensesIntro.cn: everything 先指所有物品，再指最重要的事，最后指全部细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boxes filling a room, each with a label.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴满标签、堆满房间的纸箱。

branches.en: All objects in a place come first.
branches.cn: 一个地方的所有物品是首要含义。

branches.en: The word can name what matters most.
branches.cn: 这个词能指最重要的事。

branches.en: It can also mean all the details.
branches.cn: 它也能指所有细节。

branches.en: Objects and values share one total word.
branches.cn: 物品与价值共用一个表示全部的词。

branches.en: Things and facts are both included.
branches.cn: 物品与事实都被包含。

intro.en: Everything is a compound of every and thing.
intro.cn: everything 是 every 与 thing 的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are English words with Germanic roots.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都是带日耳曼词根的英语词。

items.exampleCN: -thing 出现在 anything 与 something 中。

definition_en: in every place
core_image: 蒲公英的种子落在草地的每个角落
scene: 春天一到，草坡上到处都开着小黄花。When spring came, small yellow flowers bloomed everywhere on the grassy slope.
sceneCN: 这里 everywhere 是「到处」（第 1 个义项：每一个地方）；句意：春天一到，草坡上到处都开着小黄花。

senses.title: In all places
senses.definition: in every place
senses.definitionCN: 在每一个地方
senses.example: There were books everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 到处都是书。
senses.why: Every and where join place with totality.
senses.whyCN: every 与 where 结合，把地点与全部连在一起。

senses.title: Wherever one goes
senses.definition: in every situation one meets
senses.definitionCN: 所到之处
senses.example: She carried her notebook everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 她走到哪里都带着笔记本。
senses.why: The word follows a person through all places.
senses.whyCN: 这个词跟随一个人到所有地方。

senses.title: Widely seen
senses.definition: in many places, widely
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方，广泛地
senses.example: The song is heard everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌到处都能听到。
senses.why: Total place can shade into wide spread.
senses.whyCN: 地点的全部可以引申为广泛的传播。

intro.en: Everywhere joins every to where, the old question word for place.
intro.cn: everywhere 由 every 与 where（古时表示地点的疑问词）组合而成。

items.en: Hwǣr means where.
Every means each member of a set.
items.cn: every 意为集合中的每一个。

items.en: Every plus where forms everywhere.
items.cn: every 加 where 构成 everywhere。

items.en: It means in every place.
It can also mean widely.

note.en: Everywhere means all places; anywhere means any place.
note.cn: everywhere 指所有地方；anywhere 指任何地方。

entries.definition: in every part of a place
in every part of an area

normalIntro.en: Everywhere is the word that follows you to every corner.
normalIntro.cn: everywhere 是那个跟你到每个角落的词。

normal.en: Look everywhere means search all places.
normal.cn: look everywhere 意为在所有地方寻找。

normal.en: Flowers everywhere means flowers in all spots.
normal.cn: flowers everywhere 意为到处是花。

normal.en: From everywhere means from many places.
normal.cn: from everywhere 意为来自各地。

normal.en: Everywhere else means all other places.
normal.cn: everywhere else 意为其他所有地方。

normal.en: Compare anywhere: anywhere is one possible place, everywhere is all places.
normal.cn: 对比 anywhere：anywhere 是任一地方，everywhere 是所有地方。

abstract.en: Picture dandelion seeds settling on every corner of a lawn.
abstract.cn: 想象蒲公英种子落在草坪的每个角落。

abstract.en: Imagine a sound that reaches every open window.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传到每扇敞开窗户的声音。

abstract.en: Think of a path that never leaves the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一条始终不离开同一地点的路。

examples.en: We looked everywhere for the missing key.
examples.cn: 我们到处寻找丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: There is water everywhere after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后到处都是水。

examples.en: Her name is known everywhere in the city.
examples.cn: 她的名字在城里无人不知。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「every（每个）＋ where（哪里）」——每一个地方，就是到处。

root: every（每个）＋ where（何处）→ everywhere，核心义「每一个地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Everywhere means in every place, wherever one goes, and also widely seen.
sensesIntro.cn: everywhere 指每个地方、所到之处，也指广为流传。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dandelion seeds settling on every corner of a lawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒲公英种子落在草坪的每个角落。

branches.en: All places is the core meaning.
branches.cn: 所有地方是核心含义。

branches.en: The word follows a person everywhere.
branches.cn: 这个词追随一个人到各处。

branches.en: Total place can mean wide spread.
branches.cn: 地点的全部可以表示广泛传播。

branches.en: A place and a journey both cover all spots.
branches.cn: 地点与行程都覆盖所有角落。

branches.en: Being in all places becomes being widely known.
branches.cn: 出现在所有地方就变成广为人知。

intro.en: Everywhere is a compound of every and where.
intro.cn: everywhere 是 every 与 where 的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are English words with Germanic roots.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都是带日耳曼词根的英语词。

definition_en: facts or signs that show something is true
core_image: 桌上摆着放大镜、照片和一叠文件
scene: 警方在窗台上发现一枚指纹，这成为案件的关键证据。Police found a fingerprint on the windowsill, and it became the key evidence in the case.
sceneCN: 这里 evidence 是「证据」（第 1 个义项：帮助证明某事的事实）；句意：警方在窗台上发现一枚指纹，这成为案件的关键证据。

senses.title: Proof in a case
senses.definition: facts that help prove something
senses.definitionCN: 帮助证明某事的事实
senses.example: The police collected evidence at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在现场收集证据。
senses.why: Evidence is what makes a claim visible and clear.
senses.whyCN: 证据让主张变得可见而清楚。

senses.title: A sign
senses.definition: a sign that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事属实的迹象
senses.example: There is evidence of rain in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山里有下雨的迹象。
senses.why: The word extends from courts to ordinary observation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法庭延伸到日常观察。

senses.title: To show
senses.definition: to show or prove something
senses.definitionCN: 表明或证明某事
senses.example: The results evidence a clear improvement.
senses.exampleCN: 结果显示出明显的改善。
senses.why: The noun also became a formal verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也变成了正式动词。

intro.en: Evidence comes from Latin evidentia, clearness, from evidens, clearly seen.
intro.cn: evidence 源自拉丁语 evidentia（清楚），来自 evidens（清楚可见的）。

items.en: Videre means to see.
Evidens means clearly seen.
Evidentia means clearness.
French evidence carries the sense of proof.
items.cn: 法语 evidence 带有证明的含义。

items.en: Evidence names facts that prove something.
items.cn: evidence 指能证明某事的事实。

note.en: Evidence supports a claim; proof settles it.
note.cn: evidence 支持一个主张；proof 则能定论。

normalIntro.en: Evidence is truth laid out where everyone can see it.
normalIntro.cn: evidence 是摆出来让所有人看见的事实。

normal.en: Clear evidence leaves little doubt.
normal.cn: 明确的证据让人几乎无从怀疑。

normal.en: Evidence of rain means signs that rain fell.
normal.cn: evidence of rain 意为下过雨的迹象。

normal.en: Give evidence means tell what you know in court.
normal.cn: give evidence 意为在法庭上作证。

normal.en: Scientific evidence comes from careful tests.
normal.cn: 科学证据来自严谨的实验。

normal.en: Compare proof: evidence supports, proof settles.
normal.cn: 对比 proof：evidence 支持，proof 定论。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass over a single fingerprint.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜对准一枚指纹。

abstract.en: Imagine small marks that tell a whole story.
abstract.cn: 想象一些细小痕迹讲出完整故事。

abstract.en: Think of a light that makes a hidden fact visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一束让隐藏事实显形的光。

examples.en: The evidence supports her story.
examples.cn: 证据支持她的说法。

examples.en: Scientists found evidence of water on the planet.
examples.cn: 科学家在这颗行星上发现了水的证据。

examples.en: He gave evidence in court.
examples.cn: 他在法庭上作证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ vidence（看）」——把事实摆出来让人看见，就是证据。

root: 拉丁语 evidentia（清楚可见）← evidens（显露的）← e-（出）＋ videre（看）→ evidence。

sensesIntro.en: Evidence begins as proof in a case, extends to any sign, and then becomes a formal verb meaning to show.
sensesIntro.cn: evidence 先指案件中的证据，再指任何迹象，最后作正式动词表示表明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass, photos and papers on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的放大镜、照片与文件。

branches.en: Proof in a case is the core sense.
branches.cn: 案件中的证据是核心含义。

branches.en: Any sign can count as evidence.
branches.cn: 任何迹象都可算作证据。

branches.en: The verb means to show clearly.
branches.cn: 动词意为清楚地表明。

branches.en: Courts and daily life both read signs.
branches.cn: 法庭与日常生活都在解读迹象。

branches.en: The noun and verb share one act of showing.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共用一个展示行为。

intro.en: Evidence comes from the Latin root vid, to see.
intro.cn: evidence 来自拉丁词根 vid（看）。

latinIntro.en: Latin evidentia gives the word its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evidentia 赋予这个词形态。

items.exampleCN: evidens 由 e- 与 videre 组成。
evident 描述清楚明显的事物。

senses.title: Morally bad
senses.definition: morally wrong and cruel
senses.definitionCN: 道德上错误且残忍
senses.example: The evil king was feared by all.
senses.exampleCN: 所有人都惧怕那个邪恶的国王。
senses.why: The oldest sense is what harms others by choice.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是故意伤害他人。

senses.title: A great wrong
senses.definition: a very bad act or force
senses.definitionCN: 极坏的行为或力量
senses.example: They fought against evil in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 他们与世间的罪恶作斗争。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the force itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词变成指这种力量的名词。

senses.title: A harmful thing
senses.definition: something that causes great harm
senses.definitionCN: 造成巨大伤害的事物
senses.example: Greed is an evil that spreads quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是一种悄然蔓延的祸害。
senses.why: Any great harm can be named an evil.
senses.whyCN: 任何巨大危害都可称为祸害。

intro.en: Evil is an old English word, yfel, shared by Germanic languages.
intro.cn: evil 是古英语词 yfel，在日耳曼语族中通用。

items.en: Yfel means bad or harmful.
items.cn: yfel 意为坏的或有害的。

items.en: The word is common to Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个词在日耳曼语族中普遍存在。

items.en: Evil keeps the sense of moral harm.
items.cn: evil 保留了道德伤害的含义。

items.en: It also names the force of wrong.
Any great harm can be called an evil.
items.cn: 任何巨大危害都能称为祸害。

note.en: Evil implies deep moral wrong; bad is the general opposite of good.
note.cn: evil 指深刻的道德错误；bad 是 good 的通用反义词。

normalIntro.en: Evil is a shadow that chooses to swallow light.
normalIntro.cn: evil 是选择吞掉光明的阴影。

normal.en: An evil plan intends to hurt others.
normal.cn: an evil plan 意图伤害他人。

normal.en: Good and evil are old opposites.
normal.cn: good and evil 是古老的对照。

normal.en: An evil spirit is a harmful force.
normal.cn: an evil spirit 是害人的力量。

normal.en: The root of evil means the source of wrong.
normal.cn: the root of evil 意为罪恶的根源。

normal.en: Compare wicked: wicked stresses cruelty, evil stresses deep wrong.
normal.cn: 对比 wicked：wicked 强调残忍，evil 强调深刻的错误。

abstract.en: Picture a hand of shadow reaching through a beam of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只影子般的手穿过一束光。

abstract.en: Imagine a sweet voice that hides a sharp edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一个甜美却暗藏锋刃的声音。

abstract.en: Think of a door that opens into a very cold room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇通向极冷房间的门。

examples.en: The story is about the battle between good and evil.
examples.cn: 这个故事讲的是善与恶的斗争。

examples.en: He had an evil plan.
examples.cn: 他有一个邪恶的计划。

examples.en: The medicine left an evil taste.
examples.cn: 这药留下了一股难闻的味道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evil」倒过来是「live」——把生活颠倒，就成了 evil；这只是字母游戏，非词源。

root: 古英语 yfel（坏的）→ 中古英语 evel → evil，核心义「故意为害的」。

sensesIntro.en: Evil begins as moral badness, becomes the force of wrong, and then any great harm.
sensesIntro.cn: evil 从道德败坏开始，变成恶的力量，再指任何巨大危害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand of shadow reaching through a beam of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：影子般的手穿过一束光。

branches.en: Moral badness is the core sense.
branches.cn: 道德败坏是核心含义。

branches.en: The force of wrong becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 恶的力量成为名词。

branches.en: Any great harm can be an evil.
branches.cn: 任何巨大危害都可是祸害。

branches.en: A bad act and a bad force share one word.
branches.cn: 恶行与恶的力量共用一个词。

branches.en: Cruelty and harm are both part of evil.
branches.cn: 残忍与伤害都属于恶。

intro.en: Evil is an old English word with a Germanic root.
intro.cn: evil 是带日耳曼词根的古英语词。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Yfel is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: yfel 是现存最古老的形式。
doer 出现在 evildoer 中。

definition_en: completely correct and precise
core_image: 一把刻度清晰到毫米的尺子
scene: 木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。The carpenter measured twice before drawing the exact cutting line on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 exact 是「精确的」（第 1 个义项：每个细节都完全正确）；句意：木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。

senses.title: Completely correct
senses.definition: completely correct in every detail
senses.definitionCN: 每个细节都完全正确
senses.example: The exact time is ten past five.
senses.exampleCN: 确切时间是五点十分。
senses.why: Exact comes from Latin exigere, to weigh precisely.
senses.whyCN: exact 源自拉丁语 exigere（精确称量）。

senses.title: Strict
senses.definition: demanding great care and accuracy
senses.definitionCN: 要求高度细致准确
senses.example: The exact rules must be followed.
senses.exampleCN: 必须遵守严格的规定。
senses.why: Precise measurement becomes strict demand.
senses.whyCN: 精确的衡量变成严格的要求。

senses.title: To demand
senses.definition: to demand and obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 索取并得到某物
senses.example: The teacher exacted an apology from the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要求全班道歉。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old sense of demanding payment.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了索取偿付的旧义。

intro.en: Exact comes from Latin exactus, past participle of exigere, to drive out or weigh.
intro.cn: exact 源自拉丁语 exactus，是 exigere（驱出、称量）的过去分词。

items.en: Agere means to drive or do.
Exigere means to drive out or weigh.
Exactus means precise or exacted.
items.cn: exactus 意为精确的或被索取的。

items.en: Exact first describes precise measurement.
items.cn: exact 最初描述精确的测量。

items.en: It also means strict or demanding.

note.en: Exact stresses full correctness; precise stresses fine detail.
note.cn: exact 强调完全正确；precise 强调细节精细。

normalIntro.en: Exact is a ruler marked down to the smallest line.
normalIntro.cn: exact 是一把刻度细到最小格的尺子。

normal.en: Exact time means the precise hour and minute.
normal.cn: exact time 意为确切的小时和分钟。

normal.en: Exact words means the very words used.
normal.cn: exact words 意为原原本本的话。

normal.en: To be exact means to speak precisely.
normal.cn: to be exact 意为确切地说。

normal.en: An exact match fits perfectly.
normal.cn: an exact match 完全吻合。

normal.en: Compare precise: exact stresses no error, precise stresses fine detail.
normal.cn: 对比 precise：exact 强调无误差，precise 强调细节精细。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with marks down to a millimeter.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刻度细到毫米的尺子。

abstract.en: Imagine two puzzle pieces fitting without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图严丝合缝。

abstract.en: Think of a key that turns only in one lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只在一把锁里转动的钥匙。

examples.en: Can you give me the exact date?
examples.cn: 你能告诉我确切的日期吗？

examples.en: Those were his exact words.
examples.cn: 那就是他的原话。

examples.en: The work demands exact measurements.
examples.cn: 这项工作要求精确的测量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exact」读起来短促干脆——像尺子一下卡到位，分毫不差。

root: 拉丁语 exigere（称量、要求）→ exactus（精确的）→ exact，核心义「量得准、要求严」。

sensesIntro.en: Exact starts with complete correctness, extends to strict demands, and keeps a verb sense of demanding.
sensesIntro.cn: exact 从完全正确开始，延伸到严格要求，还保留索取的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked down to a millimeter.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度细到毫米的尺子。

branches.en: Complete correctness is the core.
branches.cn: 完全正确是核心含义。

branches.en: Precision can become strictness.
branches.cn: 精确可以变成严格。

branches.en: The verb means to demand.
branches.cn: 动词意为强求。

branches.en: A measured standard and a strict rule meet.
branches.cn: 精确标准与严格规则相遇。

branches.en: Demanding payment and exact measuring share a root.
branches.cn: 索取与精确称量共享同一个词根。

intro.en: Exact joins ex-, out, to the Latin root ag, to drive.
intro.cn: exact 由 ex-（出）与拉丁词根 ag（驱动）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exigere 是直接来源。

definition_en: in a completely correct or precise way
core_image: 两块拼图严丝合缝地扣在一起
scene: 两块拼图恰好合上，边缘没有一点缝隙。The two puzzle pieces fit exactly, with no gap at the edge.
sceneCN: 这里 exactly 是「恰好、完全准确地」（第 2 个义项：正好合适）；句意：两块拼图恰好合上，边缘没有一点缝隙。

senses.title: Precisely
senses.definition: in a completely precise way
senses.definitionCN: 以完全精确的方式
senses.example: Tell me exactly what happened.
senses.exampleCN: 把发生的事原原本本告诉我。
senses.why: The adverb describes an action done with full precision.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述以完全精确方式进行的动作。

senses.title: Just
senses.definition: used to stress that something is just right
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调正好合适
senses.example: The train arrived exactly at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 火车正好在中午到达。
senses.why: Precision in time becomes the sense of just at.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的精确变成正好在。

senses.title: Absolutely
senses.definition: used to agree strongly
senses.definitionCN: 用于强烈赞同
senses.example: That is exactly what I meant.
senses.exampleCN: 那正是我的意思。
senses.why: Complete accuracy turns into strong agreement.
senses.whyCN: 完全的准确转成强烈赞同。

intro.en: Exactly is exact plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: exactly 是 exact 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Exactus means precise.
Exact describes what is correct.
The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: Exactly often marks a precise point in time.
items.cn: exactly 常标记确切的时间点。

items.en: It is also a strong way to agree.
items.cn: 它也是强烈赞同的说法。

note.en: Exactly points to full accuracy; precisely often sounds more formal.
note.cn: exactly 指向完全准确；precisely 往往更正式。

normalIntro.en: Exactly is the click of two pieces fitting together.
normalIntro.cn: exactly 是两块拼图扣合的那一声轻响。

normal.en: Exactly right means completely correct.
normal.cn: exactly right 意为完全正确。

normal.en: Exactly the same means no difference at all.
normal.cn: exactly the same 意为毫无差别。

normal.en: Not exactly means not completely.
normal.cn: not exactly 意为不完全是。

normal.en: Exactly at noon means at twelve sharp.
normal.cn: exactly at noon 意为正午整点。

normal.en: Compare precisely: precisely is more formal, exactly is more common in speech.
normal.cn: 对比 precisely：precisely 更正式，exactly 更常出现在口语中。

abstract.en: Picture two puzzle pieces locking without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图无缝扣合。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hand stops on the very mark.
abstract.cn: 想象钟的指针正停在刻度上。

abstract.en: Think of a word that lands on the center of a target.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词正中靶心。

examples.en: The two copies look exactly alike.
examples.cn: 两份副本看起来一模一样。

examples.en: That is exactly the answer I needed.
examples.cn: 那正是我需要的答案。

examples.en: She arrived exactly on time.
examples.cn: 她正好准时到达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exact（精确的）＋ ly」——以精确的方式，就是确切地、恰好。

root: exact（精确的）＋ -ly（副词后缀）→ exactly，核心义「完全准确地」。

sensesIntro.en: Exactly marks full precision, stresses a point that is just right, and can express strong agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: exactly 标记完全精确，强调正好合适，也能表达强烈赞同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two puzzle pieces locking without a gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：严丝合缝扣在一起的两块拼图。

branches.en: Full precision is the core.
branches.cn: 完全精确是核心含义。

branches.en: Precision in time becomes just at.
branches.cn: 时间上的精确变成正好在。

branches.en: Accuracy in words becomes agreement.
branches.cn: 语言上的准确变成赞同。

branches.en: A measure and a moment can both be exact.
branches.cn: 尺度与时刻都能精确。

branches.en: Time and agreement both land on the same point.
branches.cn: 时间与赞同都落在同一点上。

intro.en: Exactly is exact plus -ly.
intro.cn: exactly 是 exact 加 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The base exact comes from Latin exactus.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 exact 来自拉丁语 exactus。
